verdict.rationale: Smithery's token-scoping docs describe service tokens restricted to connections tagged with a specific end user's metadata.userId. Combined with Smithery-managed OAuth and credential storage for connections, this delivers per-user connected accounts and per-user scoped tokens, so each user's agent acts only on that user's connections. missing for 10: detailed docs on creating and managing per-user connections at scale, independent or hands-on corroboration of the isolation.

support.subject: As a platform-engineer, I can maintain separate connected accounts and scoped tokens per end user of my product, so each user's agent acts only on that user's credentials

citations.quote: This token can list and call tools on connections in `my-app` where `metadata.userId` is `user-123` — nothing else.
Service tokens let you safely expose Smithery to browsers, mobile apps, and AI agents without leaking your API key.
Instead of implementing the MCP protocol directly, handling OAuth flows, and managing credentials yourself, Smithery handles all of it for you.
Encrypted, write-only storage for API keys and tokens
